source_title: Two boys, 16, killed in stolen car crash in Perth's north-east
source_excerpt:
Flowers have been laid on the side of Railway Parade in Bullsbrook where the two boys died. ( ABC News: Mya Kordic )
Two boys, aged 16, have died after the car they were in crashed and caught alight in Bullsbrook in Perth's north-east, while two back-seat passengers have survived.
WA Police Commissioner Col Blanch says the car was stolen, but "in no way does that lessen the tragedy".
Commissioner Blanch says it is too early to say whether the surviving passengers will face charges.
The car involved in a fiery crash which killed two 16-year-old boys in Bullsbrook in Perth's north-east on Saturday night was stolen, the police commissioner has said.
Police said the teenagers were the driver and passenger of a grey BMW 3 Series sedan that was travelling north on Railway Parade when it left the road, struck several trees and caught fire at around 10:20pm.
WA Police Commissioner Col Blanch said the car was reported stolen last night.
"In no way does that lessen the tragedy that's occurred here," Commissioner Blanch said.
"This breaks all of our hearts to know that two 16-year-old boys have died from a car accident.
"[It's] a tragedy for our community, a tragedy for the parents and families involved and for first responders … it's something that will be stuck in their brain for some time."
WA Police Commissioner Col Blanch described the crash as a tragedy. ( ABC News: Mya Kordic )
Two 17-year-old boys, who were in the back seat, were taken to Royal Perth Hospital with non life-threatening injuries.
"It's amazing that anyone walked away from that crash and we know that the crash also involved a fire that started in the brush where it crashed, so it could have been even worse," Commissioner Blanch said.
"One can only imagine, given the state of the car — I believe it was on its roof, [it] had rolled over — [that] speed was almost certainly a factor."
He said it was too early to say whether the two passengers would face charges.
Major crash investigators are examining the scene and have appealed to witnesses, or anyone with dash-cam, CCTV, or mobile phone footage related to the crash, to contact Crime Stoppers.
